brief.scenario: A 32-year-old man has a painless lump in his right testis. He is otherwise well. The examiner will show you his ultrasound report and his tumour marker results.
brief.task: Interpret the results, and answer questions on the classification, pathology and management of testicular tumours.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Read the markers first. They tell you the tumour family before the histology does.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling it a seminoma when the AFP is raised.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "An intratesticular mass with a raised AFP is a non-seminomatous germ cell tumour until proven otherwise."

grid.label: Reads the data
grid.fail: Calls it a seminoma, or ignores the AFP.
grid.pass: Intratesticular mass with raised AFP and hCG: germ cell tumour with a non-seminomatous component.
grid.high: States a significantly raised AFP means non-seminomatous management even if the histology reads seminoma.

grid.label: Classification
grid.fail: Says all testicular tumours are germ cell tumours.
grid.pass: Germ cell (seminoma and non-seminoma), sex cord-stromal (Leydig, Sertoli), lymphoma, metastases.
grid.high: Lists non-seminoma types: embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumour, choriocarcinoma, teratoma, mixed; lymphoma in older men.

grid.label: Histology
grid.fail: Cannot describe the histology of any germ cell tumour.
grid.pass: Seminoma: sheets of uniform cells with clear cytoplasm, fibrous septa with lymphocytes, sometimes granulomas.
grid.high: Yolk sac tumour: Schiller-Duval bodies. Choriocarcinoma: syncytiotrophoblast and haemorrhage. Teratoma: tissues from several germ layers.

grid.label: Tumour markers
grid.fail: Cannot say which cells produce AFP or hCG.
grid.pass: AFP from yolk sac elements, hCG from syncytiotrophoblast, LDH reflects tumour bulk. Measure before orchidectomy and repeat after.
grid.high: Half-lives: AFP 5–7 days, hCG 1–3 days; a slow fall or a rise suggests metastases; hCG can be raised in pure seminoma.

grid.label: Orchidectomy and staging
grid.fail: Plans a scrotal approach or a biopsy through the scrotum.
grid.pass: Radical inguinal orchidectomy, dividing the cord at the internal ring; contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis.
grid.high: Explains why: the testis drains to para-aortic nodes, and a scrotal incision opens a new lymphatic route to the groin.

grid.label: Treatment and fertility
grid.pass: Discusses sperm banking before treatment; treatment set by histology, stage and prognostic group.
grid.high: Stage I seminoma: surveillance preferred, or one dose of carboplatin. Stage I non-seminoma: surveillance or risk-adapted one course of BEP.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Here are his ultrasound and marker results.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: A solid mass in a young man. It's most likely a seminoma.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Describe the histology of a seminoma.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: A biopsy through the scrotum first, then decide.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Here are his ultrasound and marker results.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: There's an intratesticular mass with raised AFP and hCG. That's a germ cell tumour with a non-seminomatous component.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Germ cell tumours, divided into seminoma and non-seminoma. Then sex cord-stromal tumours such as Leydig and Sertoli cell tumours, lymphoma, and metastases.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Sheets of uniform cells with clear cytoplasm, divided by fibrous septa containing lymphocytes. There can be granulomas.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: AFP comes from yolk sac elements and hCG from syncytiotrophoblast. LDH reflects tumour bulk. They're measured before orchidectomy and repeated afterwards.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A radical inguinal orchidectomy, dividing the cord at the internal ring. Then a contrast CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis to stage.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Sperm banking before treatment. Further treatment depends on the histology, stage and prognostic group.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What if the histology comes back as pure seminoma?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: With a significantly raised AFP I'd still manage him as a non-seminomatous tumour. Pure seminoma doesn't make significant AFP.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Non-seminoma includes embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumour, choriocarcinoma, teratoma and mixed tumours. In an older man, lymphoma becomes more likely.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yolk sac tumour has Schiller-Duval bodies. Choriocarcinoma has syncytiotrophoblast and haemorrhage. Teratoma contains tissues from several germ layers.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you use the repeat markers?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: AFP has a half-life of 5 to 7 days and hCG 1 to 3 days. If they fall slowly or rise, that suggests metastatic disease. hCG can be raised in pure seminoma too.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The testis drains to the para-aortic nodes. A scrotal incision opens a new lymphatic route to the inguinal nodes.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Stage I seminoma: surveillance is preferred, or a single dose of carboplatin. Stage I non-seminoma: surveillance, or one course of BEP depending on lymphovascular invasion.

failures.move: Calling it a seminoma despite a raised AFP.

failures.consequence: Opens a second lymphatic route and complicates later treatment.
Misses fertility preservation before treatment that may affect it.

recovery.line: Germ cell or not; if germ cell, seminoma or not. The markers help decide.

knowledge.fact: Measure AFP, hCG and LDH before orchidectomy and repeat after.
Significant AFP rise in seminoma suggests a non-seminomatous component; hCG can rise in pure seminoma.
Orchidectomy dividing the cord at the internal inguinal ring is standard; discuss sperm banking before treatment.
Stage I seminoma: surveillance preferred, or one dose of carboplatin; routine adjuvant radiotherapy not recommended.

recall.think: Which markers are up, and what does that make the tumour?
do: Stage with CT; discuss sperm banking
recall.trap: A seminoma report does not override a raised AFP.
recall.finish: Treatment by histology, stage and prognostic group.

media.task: Describe the histology and name the tumour
media.description: Seminoma (clear cells with lymphocytic septa) and yolk sac tumour (Schiller-Duval body) at medium power

partner.opening: Here is his ultrasound report and his tumour markers. What do they show?

reveals.finding: Ultrasound: 2.5 cm hypoechoic, heterogeneous intratesticular mass in the right testis; left testis normal.
Markers before surgery: AFP 850 kU/L (normal under 10), hCG 120 IU/L (normal under 5), LDH 1.4 times the upper limit of normal.
CT chest, abdomen and pelvis: no enlarged nodes, no metastases.

push.question: How are testicular tumours classified?
push.expect: Germ cell (seminoma, non-seminoma), sex cord-stromal, lymphoma, metastases.

push.question: Where do AFP and hCG come from?
push.expect: Yolk sac elements; syncytiotrophoblast. Measure before and after orchidectomy.

push.question: Why is the operation inguinal?
push.expect: Para-aortic drainage; a scrotal incision adds a groin route.

push.question: What would you discuss before treatment?
push.expect: Sperm banking; plan by histology, stage and prognostic group.

curveballs.prompt: Histology says pure seminoma. Do you believe it?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not with a significantly raised AFP. Manage as non-seminomatous.

curveballs.prompt: After orchidectomy, his markers are normal. Is he cured?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not necessarily. Normal markers do not exclude metastases; staging CT and follow-up decide.

curveballs.prompt: A 70-year-old has a testicular mass. What changes?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Lymphoma becomes more likely than a germ cell tumour.
